build_note: Installed from the pinned pure-Python py3-none-any wheel by hash; the image checks that the wheel sqlparse/ package is byte-identical to the pinned sdist, that sqlparse/engine/grouping.py, sqlparse/lexer.py and the BSD-3-Clause LICENSE match recorded SHA-256 values, and that there are no unconditional runtime dependencies.
dependencies_note: atheris 3.1.0 is the in-process fuzz bridge only; sqlparse has no runtime dependencies.
parser_family: sqlparse regex lexer (sqlparse/lexer.py, keywords.py) and token-grouping engine (sqlparse/engine/grouping.py); non-validating, independent of sqlglot, libpg_query and sqlparser-rs
dialect: none selected: sqlparse has no dialect option; its lexer covers common ANSI, MySQL, PostgreSQL and Oracle keywords
api: sqlparse.parse(local SQL text decoded from UTF-8 bytes) -> tuple of grouped Statement token trees; the harness walks Statement, IdentifierList, Identifier, Function, Where, Parenthesis and Values groups and leaf token types
coverage: Python line tracing of the sqlparse package source during valid-control replay; Atheris import instrumentation for the byte-input bridge
scope: One SQL statement from local text via sqlparse.parse; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls only, each matching the hand-written oracle summary. sqlparse is a non-validating parser: it groups tokens into a tree but accepts syntactically invalid SQL, so acceptance says nothing about validity.
